name: Coolio
hook: A G-funk-era rapper whose biggest hit, built on a Stevie Wonder sample, became so famous it got parodied into an Amish comedy song against his wishes.
blurb: Coolio's 'Gangsta's Paradise' (1995), built around a sample of Stevie Wonder's 'Pastime Paradise' and written for the film 'Dangerous Minds', became one of the biggest hits of the decade. It sits at the thoughtful end of mid-1990s G-funk: its words are about violence and death, not celebrating them. Its fame made it an obvious target for a Weird Al Yankovic parody, 'Amish Paradise' (1996). Yankovic's team says permission came through Coolio's record label. Coolio said for years that he had never been asked personally and would have said no, and that he was upset when he first heard it, feeling his serious song had been turned into a joke. That objection carried weight because the parody treats the song as any hit rather than dealing with what it was about. Coolio died in September 2022.

signatureTracks.title: Gangsta's Paradise
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Built on a Stevie Wonder sample, written for 'Dangerous Minds', and one of the biggest-selling singles of the 1990s.

signatureTracks.title: Fantastic Voyage
